text:
eva: ran a perf sweep this morning across kernel selection + microbatch sizes, focusing on prefill vs decode breakdown. results are surprising — prefill is dominating for short prompts on some kernels :eyes:
cheng: can you paste the breakdown? are you measuring per-token or end-to-end latency?
eva: per-request end-to-end, plus per-token averages. reproduced on rtx-6000 and gpus with our autotuned kernels. command used:
```
./tools/perf_sweep --kernel auto --batches 1,4,8 --profile prefill,decode --duration 120s --out /tmp/sweep.json
```
eva: sample output (microbatch=1, kernel=auto):
```
summary:
 qps=72
 p50=180ms p95=320ms p99=620ms
 prefill_total: p50=45ms p95=110ms p99=240ms
 decode_total: p50=120ms p95=180ms p99=360ms
 per_tok(prefill)=0.9ms per_tok(decode)=2.4ms
 kv_hit_rate=0.88
```
eva: microbatch=4 (same kernel):
```
 qps=240
 p50=250ms p95=420ms p99=900ms   # tail shot up
 prefill_total: p50=50ms p95=125ms p99=260ms
 decode_total: p50=160ms p95=300ms p99=700ms
```
sam: interesting — throughput scales but p99 explodes. do we know if tail is coming from decoding stalls or from prefill jitter (kv misses causing re-prefill)?
eva: i pulled a flamegraph. decode time has a longer tail when we hit a fallback kernel path (quantized fallback) — shows up as long-host-calls inside fused-gemm. prefill tail correlates with KV cache eviction spikes on multi-tenant runs.
alex: that matches the recent regression we saw after the kernel selector change. When selector flips to the new heuristic under load it sometimes picks a fallback kernel for 4/8 batch sizes (latency vs memory heuristic). fallback kernel is ~2x slower in the hot path.
cheng: can we force the old kernel for a quick experiment and compare p95/p99? if p99 drops we pin and fix selector later.
eva: tried that: microbatch=4 + kernel=legacy -> p95 down to 360ms p99=480ms vs auto p99=900ms. so selector is the culprit.
sam: ok, short-term: pin legacy for the slo tier. medium-term: adjust selector to prefer decoding-stable kernels for our p99 SLO class and prefer memory-efficient kernels for throughput-only classes.
alex: also need to address KV behavior: on multi-turn traces we're seeing 10-15% extra prefill work due to partial cache misses — root cause is cache shard rebalancing at heavy QPS. solution candidates: more aggressive local caching, sticky routing by conversation id, or increasing per-shard capacity.
eva: i ran a KV-only stress test: eviction spikes when concurrent convs > 1200, eviction_rate jumps and prefill p95 increases ~30%. logs: ```kv.evictions/sec=85 -> prefill.p95 +32%```
infra-bot: perf-bench-job #2245 finished. artifacts: https://ci.internal/redwood/artifacts/2245 (includes full traces + flamegraphs).
cheng: for the SLO sweep we should produce a matrix: microbatch x kernel x kv_mode (sticky vs default). collect p50/p95/p99 + qps + kv_hit_rate. i'll open a ticket.
eva: opened RFC-1245 (link in thread) with initial data and action items. short list: (1) hotfix: pin kernel for slo route (2) tune selector heuristic to bias decode latency stability (3) KV sticky routing spike mitigation (4) add a lightweight per-request prefilling timeout to prevent long prefills from blowing p99.
sam: can we also try cooperative decode offload (stream decode ops across two kernels) as a perf experiment? might reduce decode tail for long outputs.
eva: noted. i'll schedule experiments tomorrow and attach new perf sweep results. thanks all :thumbsup:
